messages:
Emma (Marketing): Quick sync — want to lock hero + primary CTA for Hosted API / Dedicated / Private pages before we push the launch post. Can we keep this short and make routing consistent?
Jason (Growth): yes, needed for the blog + webinar landing. main asks: 1) messaging parity, 2) clear routing for inbound leads, 3) benchmark callout placement.
Liam (Product): Agree. We should highlight the decision criteria matrix: speed vs cost vs isolation. Short line per mode.
Priya (Design): I can mock 3 micro-variations of the hero (one row for each mode) — do we want a single hero that speaks to all 3 or mode-specific heroes?
Noah (Content): My vote: single hero for top-level pages (broad value prop), then a tab/anchor that switches to mode-specific headlines and CTAs. That keeps SEO and reduces bounce.
Emma (Marketing): ok — single hero, but we need 3 distinct CTAs that route to mode-specific lead flows. Hosted -> sign up, Dedicated -> talk to sales, Private -> request demo / compliance contact.
Jason (Growth): inbound routing details: Hosted signups go to self-serve funnel (utm=hosted). Dedicated leads -> SDR queue (tag: dedicated). Private -> enterprise queue w/ compliance flag. Can we capture model use-case in lead form?
Liam (Product): add a quick checkbox: "Regulated data / requires on-prem or VPC" — that auto-tags Private. Keep form 3 fields for Dedicated.
Priya (Design): mockups will include 3 CTAs visually stacked on mobile so they're clear. Also propose a small benchmark ribbon under hero: "Avg latency 60–120ms | 3x throughput vs baseline" — is that ok?
Noah (Content): Benchmarks need context. Suggest: "Real-world median latency on popular open models — tested on 8x A100 workloads" or simpler: "Latency and throughput optimized for production." We can place the detailed benchmark panel lower on the page with a link to the benchmark post.
Emma (Marketing): good call. For the hero copy drafts:
- option A (single line): "Predictable, production-grade LLM inference — hosted, dedicated, or private."
- option B (value-first): "Ship LLM features with predictable latency, cost controls, and enterprise-grade isolation."
Noah (Content): I prefer B but shorten: "Ship LLM features with predictable latency, cost, and enterprise isolation."
Priya (Design): prefer shorter lines. Also propose microcopy for CTAs:
- Hosted: "Get started — free credits"
- Dedicated: "Reserve capacity"
- Private: "Request private deployment"
Liam (Product): For routing test, CTA buttons should have data-attributes: data-mode=hosted/dedicated/private so analytics can split.
Emma (Marketing): we'll need UTM templates for blog/webinar links. Jason can you confirm the UTM params?
Jason (Growth): using utm_source=redwood_blog, utm_campaign=tri_mode_launch, utm_content=hosted|dedicated|private as appropriate. I'll add the link mapping.
Noah (Content): Webinar hook copy — put a secondary line under hero: "Live benchmarking + migration patterns — join the webinar" with a small date pill. CTA: "Register — seats limited"
Emma (Marketing): great. For the blog launch post we'll call out 3 customer stories (early hosted user, Dedicated pilot, Private compliance proof). Noah can draft.
Noah (Content): drafting now. Will include a short benchmark table and links to the webinar signup.
Priya (Design): deliverables: hero mock + mobile spacing + CTA states + benchmark ribbon treatment by EOD tomorrow.
Liam (Product): I'll wire up the routing spec in the docs repo and add the form fields. ETA 48h.
Jason (Growth): SDR mapping / tags will be in the CRM doc. I'll create automation for Private leads to notify security engineering for inbound compliance follow-up.
Emma (Marketing): action items: Noah - blog + webinar copy draft (tomorrow morning). Priya - mockups (EOD tomorrow). Liam - routing spec (48h). Jason - UTM & CRM mappings (today). I'll assemble final hero copy options and run a quick micro-test of CTAs in the staging site.
launchbot: deploy-checklist completed for marketing assets, staging build queued :rocket:
Priya (Design): quick question — should the benchmark ribbon link to a full benchmarking page or inline modal?
Noah (Content): modal ok for quick read, but SEO and shareability: separate page is better. We'll link the ribbon to the benchmark post.
Emma (Marketing): agreed. Let's keep hero lean, ribbon links out. If anyone has strong objections to any CTA wording, flag now.
Jason (Growth): no objections from growth. :thumbsup:
Liam (Product): LGTM
Priya (Design): :+1:
Noah (Content): will post draft in #marketing-drafts and ping here when ready.
Emma (Marketing): thanks team — will confirm final hero line after Noah's draft.
